Cytokeratin immunoreactivity, specifically cytokeratin 7 and/or 20 patterns, can be a useful marker for diagnosing short-segment Barrett's oesophagus in Korea. Studies have shown that a pattern of positive cytokeratin 7/20 is associated with an increased risk of developing short-segment Barrett's oesophagus.

In the context of Korean patients, this diagnostic approach may be particularly relevant due to the country's distinct genetic and environmental factors. Further research is needed to fully understand the utility of this marker in Korean populations, as well as to investigate any potential differences in tumor characteristics between Korea and other countries.

However, for non-Korean patients or those not familiar with these specific markers, cytokeratin immunoreactivity may still be a valuable tool for diagnosing short-segment Barrett's oesophagus. It is essential to note that the accuracy of this diagnostic approach can depend on various factors, such as tumor location and quality.

In summary, while cytokeratin immunoreactivity has shown promise in Korean patients with short-segment Barrett's oesophagus, more research is required to fully understand its utility and potential limitations. It is crucial to consult with a healthcare professional for accurate diagnosis and guidance on management.
